github.updatePath: in-app direct MSIXBundle download -> SHA-256 verification -> Authenticode/MSIX signature verification -> Windows package deployment -> restart

microsoftStore.publicVersionAuthority: Partner Center and the Microsoft Store client

releasePolicy.github: formal releases may be published more frequently after release approval and validation
releasePolicy.microsoftStore: stable versions are submitted only with explicit release approval; there is no longer a fixed x.0.0/x.5.0 milestone rule

github.validation: validated and frozen; v1.9.3 does not change application update download, verification, deployment, or restart behavior
github.policy: validated / frozen; future updater mechanism changes require a proven bug, security issue, or Windows platform/API compatibility requirement plus end-to-end regression evidence

microsoftStore.validation: validated and frozen; v1.9.3 does not change the Store download/install operation or its update-session behavior
microsoftStore.policy: validated / fully frozen after the successful real Microsoft Store 1.7.4 to 1.7.5 E2E acceptance on 2026-08-14; future updater mechanism changes require a proven bug, security issue, or Windows / Microsoft Store platform/API compatibility requirement plus end-to-end regression evidence on the affected channel. One user action invokes the Windows-native combined download-and-install operation; register Windows restart recovery before it starts, use app restart only when the process survives, and keep Store and GitHub identities separate

documentation.storePublicationAuthority: Partner Center and Microsoft Store availability
documentation.runtimeUpdateManifest: docs/update-manifest.json is runtime/update infrastructure and is not the documentation source of truth

priorities: keep documentation governance and current-state metadata single-sourced
preserve the frozen updater mechanism and reopen it only for a proven bug, security issue, or Windows platform/API compatibility requirement with end-to-end regression evidence
standardize tool-page layout, state presentation, responsive behavior, and accessibility
keep project organization lightweight and avoid forcing independent tools into a single workflow
formalize project and backup schema migration contracts
establish startup, package-size, dependency, and native-component budgets
then deepen GIS/data interoperability and planning-specific productivity tools
